Week 2 · A1 · Beginner

Le, la, un, une

Every French noun is masculine or feminine, and the little word in front of it tells you which.

Pick a noun, then switch between “the” and “a”, and between one and several.

Learn every noun with its article: not “maison” but “la maison”.

French has two genders, masculine and feminine. Things have a gender too, and it is mostly arbitrary: le livre (the book) is masculine, la maison (the house) is feminine. The article in front of the noun carries the gender, so learn the two together from day one.

Pattern

masculinefemininebefore a vowel or silent hplural
the (definite)le livrela maisonl’ami, l’écoleles livres
a / some (indefinite)un livreune maisonun ami, une écoledes livres

Plural nouns usually add an -s that you can’t hear. You hear the plural in the article instead: le livre sounds like “luh”, les livres like “lay”. Before a vowel, the s of les and des links to the next word: les‿amis sounds like “lay-zami”. This is called liaison.

Some clues to gender: nouns ending in -tion, -té, -ure are usually feminine (la nation, la liberté); nouns ending in -ment, -age are usually masculine (le moment, le fromage).

Examples

No French voice was found on this device, so the ▶ écouter buttons are hidden.

  • Le café est chaud. The coffee is hot.
  • La gare est loin. The station is far.
  • J’ai un frère et une sœur. I have a brother and a sister.
  • L’école est fermée aujourd’hui. The school is closed today.
  • Les enfants jouent dans le parc. The children are playing in the park.

Common mistakes

  • le école → l’école. le and la both shrink to l’ before a vowel, so you can’t see the gender. Learn it with une: une école.
  • J’ai un sœur. → J’ai une sœur. Gender follows the word, not just the person.
  • Voici livres. → Voici des livres. French almost always needs an article where English has none.
  • Talking about a job, French drops the article: Je suis professeur (I am a teacher).

Quiz

Parler: your room

A1 goal: introduce yourself and talk about your day in short, simple sentences. Look around and name five things with their article: une table, la fenêtre, un livre, les chaises, l’ordinateur. Check each gender in a dictionary (look for n.m. or n.f.).
